This one was my doing, not yours — sorry for the false alarm. The git commands I ran through the linked folder earlier today (the fetch, the fast-forward, and a status check) each created a lock file inside `.git`, and the folder mount lets git create those but not delete them, so three zero-byte leftovers — `HEAD.lock`, `index.lock` and `objects/maintenance.lock` — stayed behind. A stale `HEAD.lock` is exactly what makes `git commit` fail with "cannot lock ref 'HEAD'" (or "index.lock: File exists").

I've moved all three into `.git/stale-locks-from-claude-session-20260910/`, where git ignores them. Your repository itself is fine: HEAD and the branch still point at `a566944`, nothing was committed or lost, `git fsck` passes, and all 36 staged changes are intact. You should be able to run your commit again from Terminal now, and if you want to tidy up afterwards, `rm -r ~/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/.git/stale-locks-from-claude-session-20260910` removes the parked files.

Two small things while you're there: `papers/defect-depth/defect_depth.pdf` (your recompiled 15-page build) is now staged along with everything else, which is fine if you meant to include it; and going forward I'll keep git in this folder read-only from my side and leave committing to you, so this can't recur.
